walkthroughs.body_html: Hajj is the fifth Pillar. Every Muslim who is physically and financially able must make this pilgrimage to Mecca at least once in their life. It takes place during the Islamic month of Dhul Hijjah. Millions of Muslims gather from across the world.

Pilgrims wear simple white clothes (ihram) to show equality. They walk seven times around the Kaaba (tawaf), walk between two hills (Safa and Marwah), stand in prayer on the plain of Arafat, and symbolically stone pillars representing the devil.
Many Hajj rituals remember the prophet Ibrahim (Abraham), his wife Hajar, and his son Ismail. Hajj is also a powerful reminder that all Muslims are equal before God — rich or poor, from any country.

mcqs.q: What are the main Christian theories of atonement?
options: Jihad is the Islamic word for prayer.

Penal substitution (Christ bore the punishment for sin), Christus Victor (Christ defeated evil powers through the cross), ransom theory (Christ paid a price to free humanity), and moral exemplar (Christ's death inspires love). Different traditions emphasise different theories.
All Christians believe Jesus died only to pay God back for sin.

mcqs.q: What does the term jihad mean in Islam?
options: Jihad means 'holy war' against non-Muslims.
Jihad is the Islamic word for prayer.
Struggle or striving — the greater jihad is the internal spiritual struggle against sin; the lesser jihad refers to defensive military struggle under strict conditions.
Nirvana is the name of a Buddhist god.
